evidence: src/infrastructure/config/container.ts: buildContainer() connects InMemoryOrderRepository, InMemoryProductRepository, RandomIdGenerator and SystemClock to createCatalogueUseCases/createOrderUseCases, and loads seed data via catalogueUseCases.addProduct.execute(product). It goes through the use case instead of writing to the repository directly.
src/infrastructure/config/catalogueSeed.ts: CATALOGUE_SEED is typed as readonly AddProductCommand[], the application's own command type. Only container.ts uses it.
src/infrastructure/config/environment.ts: loadEnvironment() is the only place that checks PORT (integer from 0 to 65535) and STAFF_API_KEY, or generates a key when none is set.
Both container.ts and environment.ts are used only by src/infrastructure/main.ts, which fits a single bootstrap/config concern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files deal with one concern: configuring and starting the application. environment.ts reads and checks the process settings (port and staff API key). catalogueSeed.ts holds the start-up catalogue data. container.ts is the composition root that connects the adapters to the use cases. The files use the module's abstractions consistently: the container loads the seed data through the application's own addProduct use case instead of writing to the repository directly, so the catalogue's checks are not skipped. The seed data is typed as AddProductCommand, the application's own data shape. Each rule lives in one place: port and API-key checks only in environment.ts, wiring only in container.ts, and seed data only in catalogueSeed.ts. Nothing is duplicated and no file belongs to an unrelated concern.
